## What Is Deep Learning?

**Deep Learning** is a subset of machine learning driven by mutilayered neural networks inspired by the structure of the human brain (@ibm2025)

It is responsible for powering most forms of Artificial Intelligence.

# Deep Learning versus Neural Networks

## What is a Neural Network?

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def draw_nn(layers, labels, figsize=(8, 4.5)):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.axis("off")
    colors = ["#4C72B0"] + ["#DD8452"] * (len(layers) - 2) + ["#55A868"]

    # (x, y) position of every neuron, centered vertically in its layer
    pos = [[(i, j - (n - 1) / 2) for j in range(n)] for i, n in enumerate(layers)]

    # connections: every neuron to every neuron in the next layer
    for left, right in zip(pos[:-1], pos[1:]):
        for (x1, y1) in left:
            for (x2, y2) in right:
                ax.plot([x1, x2], [y1, y2], color="gray", lw=0.6, alpha=0.5, zorder=1)

    # neurons
    for i, layer in enumerate(pos):
        xs, ys = zip(*layer)
        ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=600, color=colors[i], edgecolor="black", zorder=2)
        ax.text(i, -max(layers) / 2 - 0.4, labels[i], ha="center", fontsize=12)

    plt.show()

draw_nn([3, 5, 5, 2], ["Input layer", "Hidden layer 1", "Hidden layer 2", "Output layer"])
```

- **Neural network:** a model that takes input data, recognizes patterns, then produces an output
- Modeled after the neurons and synapses of a human brain

## Brief History of Neural Networks

- Late 1980s: Popularized before other methods/models (e.g. SVMs, boosting, random forests) were developed
- 2000s: New methods and models outperformed and were thus preferred over neural networks
- 2010s: Repopularized after being redeveloped into *deep learning*

Source (@islp2023)

## How Do the Two Differ?

While there are a lot of overlaps and similarities, deep learning and neural networks are not inherently the same thing.

- Deep learning typically contains several layers more than neural networks
- A deep learning model must have at least 4 layers to be considered *deep*.

# Deep Learning versus Machine Learning

## How Does Deep Learning Fit Into Machine Learning?

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Circle

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))

# (radius, fill color, label, label y-position)
circles = [
    (3, "#C9D8F0", "Artificial Intelligence", 5),
    (2.2, "#F6C9A8", "Machine Learning",      3),
    (1.2, "#B9E0C1", "Deep Learning",         1),
]

for r, color, label, label_y in circles:   # largest first, so smaller ones sit on top
    ax.add_patch(Circle((0, r), r, facecolor=color, edgecolor="black", lw=1.5))
    ax.text(0, label_y, label, ha="center", va="center",
            fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")

ax.set_xlim(-3.3, 3.3)
ax.set_ylim(-0.3, 6.3)
ax.set_aspect("equal")   # keeps circles round instead of oval
ax.axis("off")
plt.show()
```

## Deep Learning versus Machine Learning

| | Machine Learning | Deep Learning |
|---|---|---|
| Data | Small to medium datasets | Large datasets |
| Feature Engineering | Done manually by humans | Learned automatically by the model |
| Training Time | Needs less time | Needs a lot of time |
| Complexity | Less complex | Highly complex |
| Hardware & Computing Power | CPU; needs less computing power | GPU; needs a lot of computing power |
| Interpretability | Easier | Harder (considered a *black box*) |
